ftf-written-vote-2020-08-31.receipt-1: The US vetoed S/2020/852, a Security Council draft, because it lacked a repatriation reference, viewing return to origin countries as essential. No national explanation was provided for the vote. Consequently, the Council did not adopt the draft, creating no new authority or requirements. The US stance prioritized repatriation over the proposed prosecution and reintegration strategies.
ftf-written-vote-2020-08-31.receipt-2: Russia voted in favour to elaborate existing guidance on prosecution and reintegration, yet stated the draft failed to recognize the primary importance of repatriation from Syria and Iraq. The United States cast the only negative vote, preventing adoption due to its status as a permanent member. While both nations emphasized repatriation, the US opposed the draft entirely, whereas Russia supported it despite its perceived shortcomings on this specific issue.
